key_takeaways: Passports, rings, wedding outfits, medicines and any power banks belong in the bag that stays with you, not in checked luggage.
Smartraveller says to confirm each passport is valid for at least six months beyond the end of your trip, and to allow at least six weeks for a new one.

Carry a doctor's letter with your prescriptions, check each medicine is legal where you are going, and never carry PBS medicines for anyone other than yourself or an immediate family member travelling with you.
Coming home, adults can bring AUD 900 of general goods into Australia duty free, cash of AUD 10,000 or more must be declared, and food and plant material must be declared or binned on arrival.
Ask your planner, venue or vendors who handles steaming, welcome bags, the wet-weather plan and luggage transfers, and get the answers in writing before you fly.

faq.q: Should I carry my wedding dress on the plane or check it in?
faq.a: Keep it with you wherever you can. It is one of the few things that cannot be replaced at the other end. Check garment bags with your airline, and since Smartraveller notes policies often limit each valuable item's value, check your item limit.

faq.q: Can I bring my wedding bouquet or flowers back into Australia?
faq.a: Declare it. On arrival you must declare risk goods, including food and plant material, or dispose of them in the airport bins; declared goods are inspected and may be treated, exported or destroyed. If a keepsake matters, plan it with your florist and photographer before the wedding.

faq.q: What should guests pack for a destination wedding?
faq.a: An outfit for each event in its dress code, shoes that suit the ground at each venue, sun protection and a light evening layer, with passport, insurance details and medicines in carry-on. Older guests should add flat shoes with grip and a doctor's letter.

faq.q: Can I take my prescription medication overseas for the wedding?
faq.a: Yes. Smartraveller says to check your medicine is legal and available where you are going and to carry copies of your prescription and a doctor's letter. The TGA notes some medicines, such as those containing codeine, may need a permit or not be allowed.

faq.q: What goes in a wedding day emergency kit?
faq.a: A sewing kit, fashion tape, stain remover, blotting papers, pain relief, plasters, snacks and water, a charged phone and charger, the vow cards, and envelopes for any tips agreed in advance. Give it to one named person, so it is never left upstairs.
